samples.summary: Cross-sheet formula resolver builds a merge cover map from the raw CRDT merge map, bypassing every clamp `rebuildMergeCoverMap` just gained
samples.evidence: `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:880-913) now spends `mergeBudgetAdmits`, try/catches `parseRef`, and rejects keys that do not round-trip through `toSref` — explicitly because anyone holding `rw` on the document can put an arbitrary merge map into the plain CRDT field. `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1235-1246` performs the *same* covered-cell walk over another tab's `ws.merges` read straight from `doc.getRoot()`: `Object.entries(ws.merges)` (not `safeWorksheetRecordEntries`, which the rest of that file uses for exactly the duplicate-key hazard), an unguarded `parseRef(anchorSref)`, and an unbounded `for r < anchorRef.r + span.rs / for c < ... + span.cs` nested loop. A single `{rs:1000000, cs:18278}` span — the case the new test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:66 asserts the engine now drops — freezes the tab here for 1.8e10 iterations, and a `__proto__`/`A1:B2` key throws out of the resolver, breaking every cross-sheet formula. The guard belongs on this site too (reuse `mergeBudgetAdmits` + `safeWorksheetRecordEntries`, or read the clamped map from `Sheet.getMerges()`).

samples.summary: `parseFreeze`'s ceiling drops from the grid bound to 1000, so freezes the editor can still create can no longer be written or round-tripped through the v1 API / CLI
samples.evidence: `parseFreeze` now caps `rows`/`cols` at `MaxSnappedFreeze` (1000) instead of MaxRows/MaxColumns. Nothing else was tightened to match: `Sheet.setFreezePane` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:543) passes a caller-requested line through untouched (the snap only bounds *growth*), and the editor reaches it with an arbitrary index at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:2974 (`this.setFreezePane(targetIndex, ...)` — freeze up to the clicked row). So a document can legitimately hold `frozenRows: 5000`, and `GET .../freeze` → `PUT .../freeze` now 400s at packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-view.ts:105-134 (`wafflebase sheets freeze set`) and for any other API client, with no migration path and no mention of the new bound in docs/design/cli.md:1620 or the CLI schema registry (packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:1195).

samples.summary: Template seeding writes `frozenRows` directly, bypassing both the new freeze ceiling and the snap invariant the API now enforces
samples.evidence: `worksheet.frozenRows = content.frozenRows ?? 0;` (packages/backend/src/template/seed/seed-templates.ts:140, values supplied by packages/backend/src/template/seed/catalog/sheets.ts:22/56/137) is a third writer of the field that `PUT .../freeze` now runs through `snapFreezePastMerges` and `parseFreeze`. Today's catalog values (1) are harmless, but this path can seed a freeze past `MaxSnappedFreeze` or one that straddles a seeded merge — the state the diff's own docs say `PUT merges`, `PUT freeze` and `POST move` all refuse to create.

samples.summary: Legacy shape migration copies the merge map wholesale, bypassing the new merge budget every other writer now spends
samples.evidence: `cloneMergeRecord` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-shape-migration.ts:87-94) rebuilds `merges` from a legacy document with no `mergeBudgetError`/`mergeBudgetAdmits` check, while the diff added that budget to `parseMerges`, the XLSX importer, `YorkieStore.setMerge` and `Sheet.canMergeSelection`. A migrated legacy tab can therefore land in the CRDT over `MaxMergeEntries`/`MaxMergeCoveredCells`; clients then silently drop merges at load (`rebuildMergeCoverMap`) and the map can never be rewritten through `PUT merges`, which would reject it.

samples.summary: Concurrency fuzz driver ignores the new `moveRows`/`moveColumns` boolean, so a refused reorder is recorded as applied
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/test/helpers/concurrency-driver.ts:52-55 `await sheet.moveRows(op.src, op.count, op.dst)` / `moveColumns(...)` discard the return value the diff introduced. `moveCells` now returns `false` and writes nothing for a move that would park a merged block across a frozen boundary (`merge-move-frozen`), so any driver-generated op combining a freeze with a merge silently diverges from the model the harness compares against.

samples.summary: `ReadOnlyStore.setMerge` now returns false, which changes read-only surfaces from 'merge applied in memory' to 'merge silently refused'
samples.evidence: `Sheet.mergeSelection` now early-returns at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4969 when the store refuses, and `applyPasteMerges`/`moveRangeTo` `continue` past a refused block. With `ReadOnlyStore` (used by packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/lakehouse-view.tsx:40) every merge write now reports failure where it previously updated `Sheet.merges` in memory. Probably the intended behaviour for a read-only view, but it is a behaviour change at a consumer outside the diff and worth a conscious confirmation.

verdict.reason: All cited evidence checks out against the repository. sheet.ts:880-917 shows rebuildMergeCoverMap now spending mergeBudgetAdmits (887), try/catching parseRef (889-896), and rejecting non-round-tripping keys (900), with a doc comment (862-872) stating the threat is an arbitrary merge map injected into the plain CRDT field by any rw holder. sheet-view.tsx:1234-1246 is a second reader of that same raw field (ws from doc.getRoot() at 1231) performing the identical covered-cell walk with none of the three clamps: plain Object.entries (1236) instead of safeWorksheetRecordEntries (which exists at worksheet-record.ts:47-61 for the duplicate-own-keys throw and is used for ws.merges at yorkie-store.ts:1072 and worksheet-structure.ts:279), unguarded parseRef (1237) which throws 'Invalid Reference' per coordinates.ts:350-352, and an unbounded nested loop (1238-1239) with no budget check. The exact span merge.test.ts:66 asserts is dropped ({rs:1000000, cs:18278}) walks unclamped here. This is the blast-radius lane exactly: a new guard on one reader with another reachable reader of the same untrusted data bypassing it; nothing upstream of the resolver clamps the map since it bypasses Sheet.getMerges() entirely. Major is appropriate (tab freeze / thrown cross-sheet formulas).

finding.summary: `parseFreeze`'s ceiling drops from the grid bound to 1000, so freezes the editor can still create can no longer be written or round-tripped through the v1 API / CLI
finding.evidence: `parseFreeze` now caps `rows`/`cols` at `MaxSnappedFreeze` (1000) instead of MaxRows/MaxColumns. Nothing else was tightened to match: `Sheet.setFreezePane` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:543) passes a caller-requested line through untouched (the snap only bounds *growth*), and the editor reaches it with an arbitrary index at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:2974 (`this.setFreezePane(targetIndex, ...)` — freeze up to the clicked row). So a document can legitimately hold `frozenRows: 5000`, and `GET .../freeze` → `PUT .../freeze` now 400s at packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-view.ts:105-134 (`wafflebase sheets freeze set`) and for any other API client, with no migration path and no mention of the new bound in docs/design/cli.md:1620 or the CLI schema registry (packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:1195).

verdict.reason: The code exists as described: parseFreeze caps rows/cols at MaxSnappedFreeze (1000) (worksheet-settings.ts:72-73; MaxSnappedFreeze=1000 at merging.ts:60), while every other writer of frozenRows/frozenCols is unbounded by that ceiling. snapFreezePastMerges only releases an axis when the snap *grew* past the ceiling (merging.ts:361 `if (snapped !== line && snapped > MaxSnappedFreeze) return 0;`), so a caller-requested 5000 that straddles no merge passes through untouched; Sheet.setFreezePane stores it (sheet.ts:543-547) and the editor supplies an arbitrary drag-derived index (view/worksheet.ts:2971-2977, computed at 2937-2941 with no 1000 clamp), and the yorkie store writes it raw (yorkie-store.ts:1204-1219). Independently, inserting rows inside the frozen band grows the pane without a ceiling on both the editor path (sheet.ts:1446-1452) and the backend v1 structure path (worksheet-structure.ts:254-268). Therefore GET .../freeze can legitimately return >1000 (worksheet.controller.ts:92) and feeding that same value back through PUT .../freeze (worksheet.controller.ts:106) or `wafflebase sheets freeze set`, which forwards the body untouched (cli/src/commands/sheets-view.ts:105-141), now 400s. No guard, clamp, or migration elsewhere prevents the out-of-range stored state, so none of not-present/already-guarded applies, and a stricter validation breaking other entry points' round-trip is exactly the blast-radius lane (major: a site left broken).
